**England vs DR Congo (FIFA World Cup 2026, Round of 32, scheduled for around July 1, 2026, at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, USA) – pre-match factors as of June 27, 2026.**[[1]](https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/england-dr-congo-world-cup-preview/blt5d30fa324b3ac0ec)[[2]](https://sports.yahoo.com/soccer/article/2026-fifa-world-cup-daily-schedule-every-match-date-kickoff-time-and-venue-for-all-48-teams-234515087.html)

All information below draws exclusively from sources published on or before June 27, 2026 (or historical facts known well before). Post-June 27 match outcomes, scores, or events are ignored entirely. ### Head-to-Head History
England and DR Congo (Democratic Republic of the Congo) had **no recorded prior meetings** in international football (senior men's matches, including friendlies or major tournaments). Their Round of 32 clash was set to be the first-ever encounter.[[3]](https://tips.gg/article/england-vs-d-r-congo-head-to-head-record-stats-form-updated-june-2026/)

### Recent Form and Results (Leading into Late June 2026)
- **England (Group L)**: Strong start with a 4-2 win over Croatia (mid-June, featuring goals from Harry Kane and others). Followed by a 0-0 draw against Ghana (June 23). By June 27, England had secured qualification for the knockout stage (at worst as one of the best third-placed teams, with potential for top spot depending on the final group match vs Panama on June 27). Earlier warm-up friendlies included 3-0 vs Costa Rica and 1-0 vs New Zealand (early June).[[4]](https://www.olympics.com/en/news/england-fifa-world-cup-2026-three-lions-results-scores-standings-full-list)[[5]](https://www.espn.co.uk/football/team/results/_/id/448/eng)[[6]](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/27/england-through-to-last-32-of-the-world-cup-after-uruguay-exit-against-spain)
- **DR Congo (Group K)**: First World Cup appearance since 1974 (over 50 years). Overall qualifying record (including playoffs): approximately 10 wins, 2 losses, 1 draw, with 18 goals scored and 7 conceded.[[7]](https://www.si.com/soccer/dr-congo-2026-world-cup-preview)[[8]](https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/world-cup-2026-group-k-200000651.html)
  - Pre-tournament form included a 1-0 AFCON 2025 round-of-16 loss to Algeria (January 2026, without several injured players) and friendlies such as 2-0 vs Bermuda and 1-0 vs Jamaica (early 2026). They had a limited scoring record, failing to score more than one goal in eight of their last 10 matches before the tournament.[[7]](https://www.si.com/soccer/dr-congo-2026-world-cup-preview)
  - In the group stage (matches known by mid-to-late June): 1-1 draw with Portugal (June 17); 0-1 loss to Colombia.[[9]](https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/congo-england-ghana-round-up-review-highlights)

### Injuries and Suspensions
- **England**: Reece James suffered a hamstring injury in the closing stages of the 0-0 draw with Ghana (June 23). As of the June 27 report, he was ruled out for the final group match against Panama and the subsequent Round of 32 tie against DR Congo. Jarell Quansah was also noted as unavailable for the knockout match in some reporting.[[6]](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/27/england-through-to-last-32-of-the-world-cup-after-uruguay-exit-against-spain)[[10]](https://www.skysports.com/football/news/12098/13559299/england-2026-world-cup-news-reece-james-and-jarell-quansah-to-miss-last-32-clash-vs-dr-congo-with-injury)
- **DR Congo**: No major specific injury concerns highlighted in pre-tournament previews, though the side had dealt with absences during AFCON.[[11]](https://totalfootballanalysis.com/competitions/fifa-world-cup-2026/dr-congo-world-cup-odds-predictions)

### Travel, Fatigue, and Venue Conditions
- **Venue**: Mercedes-Benz Stadium, Atlanta, USA (modern NFL stadium with retractable roof, likely providing climate control for the hot/humid June-July Atlanta summer conditions).[[1]](https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/england-dr-congo-world-cup-preview/blt5d30fa324b3ac0ec)
- **DR Congo advantage**: Their final group match vs Uzbekistan was scheduled in Atlanta on June 27. This meant minimal additional travel or fatigue for the Round of 32 fixture in the same venue just days later.[[12]](https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/jun/27/dr-congo-v-uzbekistan-world-cup-2026-live)
- **England**: Coming off matches in various US venues (e.g., Dallas/Arlington area for Croatia, Boston area for Ghana, New Jersey for Panama). Transcontinental or cross-US travel to Atlanta would be more significant than DR Congo’s situation. - Pitch expected to be high quality (standard for the stadium). Crowd would be in a neutral US venue, though England typically draws strong traveling support, and DR Congo could benefit from diaspora fans. ### Other Notable Storylines
- DR Congo’s participation marked a historic return to the World Cup after more than five decades, with a squad featuring several players with European (including Premier League) experience, such as Yoane Wissa, Aaron Wan-Bissaka, and Axel Tuanzebe. Coach Sébastien Desabre emphasized a balanced 4-at-the-back setup capable of defensive solidity or quick transitions.[[8]](https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/world-cup-2026-group-k-200000651.html)
- England, managed by Thomas Tuchel, entered as heavy favorites but faced right-back depth concerns due to the James injury. The team had shown attacking potency (e.g., Kane’s contributions) alongside occasional defensive resilience in draws.[[6]](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/27/england-through-to-last-32-of-the-world-cup-after-uruguay-exit-against-spain)

These factors (especially the lack of H2H, DR Congo’s venue familiarity/fatigue edge, England’s injury issues at right-back, and the historic context for DR Congo) provided context beyond baseline team rankings/strength for pre-match analysis.

factors.impact: Reece James' hamstring injury rules him out for the Round of 32, creating a notable right-back depth concern for England. This is a tangible weakening of a key position.
DR Congo's final group match was in Atlanta, meaning they face minimal travel to the Round of 32 venue, offering a clear rest and familiarity advantage over England's cross-US travel.
With no prior meetings, there is no historical precedent to inform or adjust the prediction based on past matchups.

DR Congo struggled offensively pre-tournament, failing to score more than one goal in eight of their last 10 matches, and scored only twice in their two known World Cup group games (1-1 draw vs Portugal, 0-1 loss vs Colombia). This suggests a potential challenge against a strong England defense.

England secured knockout qualification with a strong start, including a 4-2 win over Croatia, indicating good form and attacking potency. This reinforces their baseline strength but is an existing factor rather than an adjustment.

analysis.reasoning: While England enters as heavy favorites, supported by a strong start to their World Cup campaign, specific factors warrant a moderate downward adjustment to their predictive advantage. The most significant is the injury to key right-back Reece James, compounded by Jarell Quansah's unavailability, which creates a tangible depth concern for England's defense in a crucial knockout match. Furthermore, DR Congo benefits from a notable travel and fatigue advantage, having played their final group match in the same Atlanta venue, minimizing their preparation demands compared to England's more extensive cross-US travel. Although DR Congo's recent scoring record suggests they might struggle to break down England, these mitigating factors for England collectively warrant an adjustment favoring DR Congo to a conservative degree, bringing the teams slightly closer than a raw baseline might suggest.
